US president calls it ‘foolish violation’ of ceasefire agreement after drone damaged ship’s upper deck Donald Trump on Friday blamed Iran for carrying out a drone strike on a cargo ship in the strait of Hormuz, calling it a “foolish violation” of the ceasefire agreement with the US. One drone damaged the upper deck of the ship but the ship was able to proceed, the US president said. The US shot down three other drones aimed at the ship, he said. His post on social media did not identify the ship or the time of the strike, but on Thursday the British military said a vessel was hit by a projectile off the coast of Oman.

A fragile interim ceasefire between the United States and Iran faced a major disruption Friday after a cargo ship was damaged by a drone strike in the volatile Strait of Hormuz. U.S. President Donald Trump blamed Tehran for the incident, labeling it a “foolish violation” of the newly minted peace agreement. Writing on social media, Trump stated that a single drone hit the upper deck of the vessel. While he noted that “damage was done,” the ship was stable enough to continue its route. The U.S. military intercepted and shot down three other drones during the encounter, according to the president.

The development comes during a fragile time for the US and Iran as they work to negotiate a permanent end to the war. Iran has increasingly challenged the region and the US over its control of the strait of Hormuz, even with the current interim deal it reached with the US. last week. A missile warning in the United Arab Emirates caused by a technical glitch earlier on Friday underscored the ongoing tensions in the region, following the attack on the cargo vessel and Israeli strikes in Lebanon over the past few days. The mobile phone alert startled many across the city-state of Dubai, the first such alert since the interim ceasefire.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
US president calls it ‘foolish violation’ of ceasefire agreement after drone damaged ship’s upper deck

Donald Trump on Friday blamed Iran for carrying out a drone strike on a cargo ship in the strait of Hormuz, calling it a “foolish violation” of the ceasefire agreement with the US.

One drone damaged the upper deck of the ship but the ship was able to proceed, the US president said. The US shot down three other drones aimed at the ship, he said.

His post on social media did not identify the ship or the time of the strike, but on Thursday the British military said a vessel was hit by a projectile off the coast of Oman.

The development comes during a fragile time for the US and Iran as they work to negotiate a permanent end to the war. Iran has increasingly challenged the region and the US over its control of the strait of Hormuz, even with the current interim deal it reached with the US. last week.

A missile warning in the United Arab Emirates caused by a technical glitch earlier on Friday underscored the ongoing tensions in the region, following the attack on the cargo vessel and Israeli strikes in Lebanon over the past few days.

The mobile phone alert startled many across the city-state of Dubai, the first such alert since the interim ceasefire.

The brief text alert that was sent from the UAE’s interior ministry on Friday was also the first of its kind in Dubai during the Iran war. However, alerts have gone off in the region warning of incoming Iranian missiles and drones following the start of the war on 28 February, when the US and Iran launched their strikes on Iran.

A short time after the alert, the Emiratis said there was a telephone call between the foreign minister, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and the Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi. It quoted Sheikh Abdullah as telling Araghchi that the UAE “emphasized the importance of full commitment” to the interim deal between Iran and the US.

“Serious diplomacy and responsible dialogue are the optimal path for addressing all regional and international crises,” it said.

The US and Iran are still negotiating terms of the interim peace deal, including issues such as getting ships through the key strait and addressing the future of Iran’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium. Under the interim deal, the two sides have 60 days to work out the details.

A fragile interim ceasefire between the United States and Iran faced a major disruption Friday after a cargo ship was damaged by a drone strike in the volatile Strait of Hormuz. U.S. President Donald Trump blamed Tehran for the incident, labeling it a “foolish violation” of the newly minted peace agreement.

Writing on social media, Trump stated that a single drone hit the upper deck of the vessel. While he noted that “damage was done,” the ship was stable enough to continue its route. The U.S. military intercepted and shot down three other drones during the encounter, according to the president.

The social media post did not identify the targeted ship or specify the exact timing of the attack. However, the details align with a report from the British military on Thursday, which stated that a vessel had been struck by an unknown projectile off the coast of Oman.

The timing of the strike comes at a critical juncture for both nations. The U.S. and Iran are currently inside a 60-day window to negotiate a permanent end to the war that began on February 28. Current negotiations are heavily focused on securing safe passage through key maritime shipping lanes and addressing the future of Iran’s highly enriched uranium stockpile.

Adding to regional anxieties on Friday afternoon, a sudden mobile phone alert flashed across screens in Dubai warning residents of an incoming missile. The message, sent by the United Arab Emirates’ Interior Ministry, caused immediate concern across the city-state before officials issued a swift retraction. Authorities instructed the public to “disregard the previous warning,” later clarifying that the alert was triggered entirely by a technical malfunction.

The false alarm prompted immediate high-level diplomatic contact. payload.title: Trump syyttää Irania drooni-iskusta rahtialukseen Hormuzinsalmessa
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain presidentin Donald Trumpin mukaan Iran teki drooni-iskun rahtialukseen Hormuzinsalmessa ja rikkoi näin väliaikaista tulitaukoa Yhdysvaltojen kanssa.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump syytti perjantaina Irania drooni-iskusta rahtialukseen Hormuzinsalmessa, jossa yksi drooni vaurioitti aluksen yläkantta. Trumpin mukaan alus pystyi jatkamaan matkaansa, mutta tapaus oli Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin välisen väliaikaisen tulitauon “typerä rikkomus”.

## Alus jatkoi matkaansa

Trump kertoi asiasta sosiaalisessa mediassa. Hänen mukaansa Yhdysvallat ampui alas kolme muuta droonia, joiden kohteena oli sama rahtialus. Presidentti ei viestissään nimennyt alusta eikä kertonut tarkkaa iskun ajankohtaa.

Britannian armeija oli torstaina ilmoittanut, että alus oli osunut ammukseen Omanin rannikon edustalla. Lähdetietojen perusteella tapaus sijoittuu samaan alueelliseen jännitteeseen, mutta Trumpin viestissä ei yksilöity alusta tavalla, joka vahvistaisi kaikkia yksityiskohtia.

## Tulitauko joutui paineeseen

Välikohtaus tapahtui hauraassa vaiheessa, sillä Yhdysvallat ja Iran olivat lähdetietojen mukaan pyrkineet neuvottelemaan pysyvämmästä ratkaisusta sodan päättämiseksi. Väliaikainen sopimus oli saavutettu viime viikolla, ja rahtialukseen kohdistunut isku nosti sen kestävyyden uudelleen esiin.

Lähdetietojen mukaan Iran on haastanut alueella Yhdysvaltoja ja muita toimijoita Hormuzinsalmen hallintaan liittyvissä kysymyksissä myös väliaikaisen sopimuksen aikana. Trumpin mukaan rahtialukseen osunut drooni aiheutti vahinkoa, mutta alus pysyi riittävän vakaana jatkaakseen reittiään.

## Alueella oli muitakin hälytyksiä

Alueen hermostuneisuutta lisäsi perjantaina myös Arabiemiirikunnissa annettu ohjusvaroitus, joka johtui teknisestä viasta. Matkapuhelimiin tullut hälytys säikäytti monia Dubaissa, ja sen kerrottiin olleen ensimmäinen tällainen varoitus väliaikaisen tulitauon jälkeen.

Lähdetiedot liittivät tunnelman kiristymiseen myös viime päivien Israelin iskut Libanonissa. Rahtialukseen kohdistunut isku osoitti, kuinka nopeasti väliaikainen sopimus voi joutua koetukselle, vaikka osapuolet ovat samalla yrittäneet hakea pysyvämpää ratkaisua.
